components.cost_effect: One projection per update; no additional cost observations.
components.name: Domain shrinkage
components.operation: Project centers to K=(1−alpha)S before adding delta u_t.
components.requires: Convex S, rB_d⊆S, 0<alpha<1 and delta≤alpha r.
transfer_checks: Re-establish feasibility if perturbation geometry or feasible-set access changes.

components.cost_effect: Exactly one played-point value per round; no second-point baseline query.
components.goal: Simulate a gradient of ball smoothing in conditional expectation.
components.key_estimate: Source Lemma 1 supplies the smoothed-gradient identity; ||g_t||≤dC/delta in the performance proof.
components.name: One-value sphere direction
components.operation: Use c_t(y_t+delta u_t)u_t in the update; its analytic rescaling is g_t=(d/delta)c_t(x_t)u_t.
components.requires: Fresh uniform sphere u_t independent of the fixed loss sequence, bounded absolute losses and a feasible perturbation ball.
transfer_checks: Noisy feedback or other perturbation laws require a new mean/size argument; arbitrary-function regularity is not certified.

content.family: Uniform ball smoothing, sphere-value estimation and domain shrinkage

limitations.statement: This is a selected Algorithm upper-bound witness against an oblivious sequence, not a lower bound for unrestricted algorithms or a claim of optimal Oracle Complexity.
Exact projection is an additional capability; one cost value per round does not make the full implementation evaluation-only.

performance_links.scope_note: Only the complete conditions, tuning, regret metric and separately charged resources of thm.P030.lipschitz_regret.

variants.cost: One exact cost observation, one independent sphere sample and one exact projection per round: n of each for literal Figure 1, including y_{n+1}. Arithmetic on d-dimensional vectors is additional; no projection runtime bound is asserted. No preprocessing or reshaping cost is folded into the value-query count.
variants.name: Figure 1 BGD with Theorem 2 Lipschitz tuning
variants.output: The online played sequence x_1,...,x_n. It is feasible because y_t∈K and K+delta B_d⊆S. The internal centers are not the played actions; no last-iterate minimizer is promised.
public_inputs: Horizon n, dimension d, feasible set S and exact projection access
Known bounds C>0, L≥0 and 0<r≤R with rB_d⊆S⊆RB_d
variants.query_and_update: For t=1,...,n independently sample u_t uniformly on {u:||u||_2=1}; play x_t=y_t+delta u_t and observe c_t(x_t). Set y_{t+1}=P_K(y_t−nu c_t(x_t)u_t). The update uses the raw value and direction: the factor d/delta belongs to the analytic estimator and is absorbed into the equivalent step size eta=nu delta/d.
variants.requirements: A fixed unknown sequence of convex L-Lipschitz functions c_t:S→[-C,C]; exact scalar feedback only at the played x_t; independent uniform Euclidean sphere sampling; exact Euclidean projection onto K.
variants.state_and_initialization: Keep y_t∈R^d; initialize y_1=0. Let K=(1−alpha)S. S is selected closed and convex with rB_d⊆S⊆RB_d.
variants.tuning_and_stopping: Set nu=R/(C sqrt(n)), delta=n^(−1/4)sqrt(R d C r/[3(Lr+C)]), alpha=delta/r; use the selected regime delta<r. Run exactly n rounds. No adaptive tuning, restart or extra evaluations are asserted.
